paper.title_en: Central rapidity jet transverse single spin asymmetry measurements in proton-proton collisions with sPHENIX
paper.abstract_en: The transverse single spin asymmetry (TSSA) in inclusive jet production at mid-rapidity has been measured in 2024 using transversely polarized proton–proton collision data collected with the sPHENIX detector at the Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collider (RHIC) at a center-of-mass energy of 200 GeV. Jets are reconstructed using the full calorimeter system with the anti-𝑘$_{T}$ algorithm and a jet cone radius of 0.4. The analysis is based on an integrated luminosity of approximately 42 pb$^{-1}$, selected from a total collected luminosity of about 107 pb$.^{-1}$. The jet energy scale and resolution are corrected using Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations, and momentum smearing effects are unfolded using an iterative Bayesian method.The TSSA is extracted from the azimuthal modulation of the jet yield asymmetry relative to the proton spin direction. The measured inclusive jet TSSA is found to be consistent with zero within statistical and systematic uncertainties over the analyzed transverse momentum range.
